items.title: Supreme Court upholds reopening of tax assessments against former CJI YK Sabharwal’s sons
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently upheld the reopening of income-tax assessments against businessmen Chetan Sabharwal and Nitin Sabharwal, sons of former Chief Justice of India late YK Sabharwal , over share transactions involving a total consideration of ₹255 crore [ Chetan Sabharwal v. ACIT, New Delhi ]. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran dismissed four appeals filed by the brothers challenging a 2019 Delhi High Court judgment that had upheld the Income Tax (IT) Department’s decision to reopen their assessments. The Court held that an investigation report pointing to the alleged overvaluation of shares constituted tangible material on the basis of which the Assessing Officer could form a reason to believe that income chargeable to tax had escaped assessment. "The expression 'reason to believe' in Section 147 of the Act means cause or justification. The Assessing Officer must have tangible material having a rational connection or a live link with the formation of the belief... items.title: Delhi Police seeks to silence digital rights groups IFF, SFLC on X, wants accounts removed
items.summary: The Delhi police has issued two notices to social media platform X, seeking the removal of the accounts of digital rights organisations Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) and Software Freedom Law Center (SFLC) apart from the operator of GeoBlockedIndia, over allegations of defamation against the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS). IFF is a digital rights advocacy organisation that defends against threats to civil liberties and democracy in India, and SFLC is a donor-supported legal services and policy organisation founded in 2010 that protects digital freedom, privacy and civil liberties in India. The IFF on Tuesday, November 3, said it would approach the court if the Delhi Police does not withdraw the notices, which also seek removal of 37 posts, including content published by 16 other users.
